q-10685.name: Question 1
q-10685.problem: What is the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=3{x}^{4}+12{x}^{2}+2\sqrt{x}$ at the point $(1,17)?$
q-10685.worked_solution:
This time, we'll use $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ notation. First, we compute the derivative, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{4}+12{x}^{2}+2{x}^{1/2}) \\  & =4\cdot 3{x}^{3}+2\cdot 12x+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2{x}^{-1/2} \\  & =12{x}^{3}+24x+{x}^{-1/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=1$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & =12(1)^{3}+24(1)+(1)^{-1/2} \\  & =12+24+1 \\  & =37.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $37.$

q-10685.html:
Question 1
?

What is the slope of the tangent to the curve y=3x4+12x2+2x at the point (1,17)?

a
40
b
451/4
c
45
d
371/2
e
37
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

This time, we'll use dydx notation. First, we compute the derivative, which gives

dydx=ddx(3x4+12x2+2x1/2)=4⋅3x3+2⋅12x+12⋅2x−1/2=12x3+24x+x−1/2. Evaluating at x=1 gives dydx|x=1=12(1)3+24(1)+(1)−1/2=12+24+1=37.

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is 37.

q-48817.name: Question 2
q-48817.problem: Find the $x$-coordinates of the points on the curve $y=-2{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+20x-1$ whose tangent has a slope of $2.$
q-48817.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=-2{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+20x-1.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+20x-1) \\  & =-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})+6\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+20\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\  & =-2\cdot 3{x}^{2}+6\cdot 2x+20\cdot 1-0 \\  & =-6{x}^{2}+12x+20.\end{aligned}
$$

We now set ${f}^{′}(x)=2$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-6{x}^{2}+12x+20 & =2 \\ -6{x}^{2}+12x+18 & =0 \\ -6({x}^{2}-2x-3) & =0 \\ -6(x+1)(x-3) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent is equal to $2$ at the points where $x=-1,3.$

Question 2
?

Find the x-coordinates of the points on the curve y=−2x3+6x2+20x−1 whose tangent has a slope of 2.

a
x=3
b
x=−3,1.
c
x=−1,3
d
x=−3
e
x=1
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let f(x)=−2x3+6x2+20x−1. The slope of the tangent at the point x is equal to f′(x). Computing the derivative, we get

f′(x)=ddx(−2x3+6x2+20x−1)=−2ddx(x3)+6ddx(x2)+20ddx(x)−ddx(1)=−2⋅3x2+6⋅2x+20⋅1−0=−6x2+12x+20.

We now set f′(x)=2 and solve for x:

−6x2+12x+20=2−6x2+12x+18=0−6(x2−2x−3)=0−6(x+1)(x−3)=0.

Therefore, the slope of the tangent is equal to 2 at the points where x=−1,3.

q-342102.name: Question 3
q-342102.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=2{x}^{5}-8{x}^{4}+24{x}^{2}-16.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=3$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(3).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{5}-8{x}^{4}+24{x}^{2}-16) \\  & =2\cdot 5{x}^{4}-8\cdot 4{x}^{3}+24\cdot 2x-0 \\  & =10{x}^{4}-32{x}^{3}+48x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=3$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(3) & =10({3}^{4})-32({3}^{3})+48(3) \\  & =810-864+144 \\  & =90.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=3$ is

$$
m={f}^{′}(3)=90.
$$

Let f(x)=2x5−8x4+24x2−16. The slope of the tangent at x=3 is equal to f′(3). Computing the derivative, we get

f′(x)=ddx(2x5−8x4+24x2−16)=2⋅5x4−8⋅4x3+24⋅2x−0=10x4−32x3+48x.
Now, we evaluate at x=3 and get f′(3)=10(34)−32(33)+48(3)=810−864+144=90.

q-342248.name: Question 4
q-342248.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+12x.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+12x) \\  & =3{x}^{2}-12x+12.\end{aligned}
$$

We now set ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-12x+12 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-4x+4 & =0 \\ (x-2)^{2} & =0 \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent is equal to $0$ at the point where $x=2.$

f′(x)=ddx(x3−6x2+12x)=3x2−12x+12.

We now set f′(x)=0 and solve for x:

3x2−12x+12=0x2−4x+4=0(x−2)2=0x=2.
